newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia domestic air activity at record.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia domestic air activity at record.

text.p: Australian airlines carried about 24.8 million revenue passengers in the year to June, up about 5.7 percent from a year earlier, the Department of Transport and Regional Development said on Monday.

Total revenue passenger kilometres increased by about 7.3 percent during the period, reflecting increased activity on long haul rights, the department said. "These results are a further indication of the steady growth in domestic aviation," it said.

Among the strongest routes, the number of passengers carried between Brisbane and Melbourne rose 13.2 percent, Coolangatta-Melbourne rose 9.7 percent and Perth-Sydney rose 8.5 percent. Australia's busiest route, Melbourne-Sydney, increased 6.8 percent to about 4.8 million passenger trips in 1995/96.
Total revenue passenger load factors averaged 72.4 percent during the 1995/96 year.
Available seat kilometres (seat capacity) increased by about 7.4 percent over the year, the department said.
